facts.headline: Money that speaks 17 languages
facts.fact: India's constitution recognises 22 languages, and every rupee banknote spells out its value in 17 of them.

facts.headline: Motorways without a speed limit
facts.fact: Long stretches of Germany's Autobahn have no general speed limit, only an advisory speed of 130 km/h.

facts.headline: A nation of 14,000 islands
facts.fact: Japan is made up of more than 14,000 islands, although most people live on the four largest.

facts.headline: Neighbour to almost everyone
facts.fact: Brazil shares a border with every country in South America except Chile and Ecuador.

facts.headline: Tallest for 3,800 years
facts.fact: The Great Pyramid of Giza was the tallest structure built by people for more than 3,800 years.

facts.headline: Two countries inside one
facts.fact: Italy completely surrounds two other independent countries: San Marino and Vatican City.

facts.headline: A lake near the clouds
facts.fact: Lake Titicaca, on Peru's border with Bolivia, lies 3,812 metres above sea level and is often called the highest navigable lake in the world.

facts.headline: Wider than the Moon
facts.fact: Mainland Australia is about 4,000 km from west to east, wider than the Moon, which is about 3,474 km across.

facts.headline: The longest coastline on Earth
facts.fact: Canada has the longest coastline of any country, stretching along the Atlantic, Pacific and Arctic oceans.

facts.headline: A parliament from the Viking age
facts.fact: Iceland's parliament, the Althing, was founded in 930 and is one of the oldest parliaments in the world.
